countries.summary: Talent-rich ecosystem centred on Buenos Aires and Córdoba that produced MercadoLibre, Globant, Ualá, Auth0 and Despegar. Strong in software, fintech, agtech and biotech, but macro volatility and capital controls shape fundraising.
countries.startup_visa: none (no startup visa; digital nomad visa and standard residence routes via Dirección Nacional de Migraciones)

countries.notes: National startup programs were cut back in 2024–2026; Fondo Semilla/Fondo Expansión no longer active as of 2026. Provincial funds (e.g. Córdoba Semilla/Triple F up to ARS 40M, closed 2026-07-08; Río Negro; San Juan) are the main public seed sources but their official URLs could not be verified, so they are omitted. Wayra Argentina site has an expired certificate and is not listed among Wayra hubs. ~ARS 1,400/US$ (volatile).

countries.summary: Largest startup ecosystem in Oceania, centred on Sydney and Melbourne with growing Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide hubs. Strong in SaaS, fintech, healthtech and deep tech; global outcomes include Atlassian, Canva, Afterpay and Airwallex.

countries.company_setup: Proprietary limited company (Pty Ltd) registered online with ASIC in about a day (fee about A$600). Needs at least one director ordinarily resident in Australia, so foreigners usually appoint a local director.
countries.notes: As of 2026-10-20: Industry Growth Program paused to new applications since 12 May 2026; EMDG Round 4 closed pending the 2026 review; R&DTI changes announced in the 2026-27 Budget take effect from 1 July 2028. LaunchVic and Breakthrough Victoria merged into Innovation Victoria on 1 July 2026. Techstars Sydney closed after NSW funding ended (no 2026 program), and the Sydney School of Entrepreneurship wound down in August 2025, so both are left out. The ICON 2026 date comes from a CBRIN article; the official page rate-limited the fetch. Antler AU cheque size is not published.

countries.company_setup: Wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) limited liability company registered with SAMR. Usually needs a local registered address and in-person or agent filings, so remote setup in practice goes through an agent. Under the 2024 Company Law, registered capital must be paid within 5 years. Takes about 1-3 months.
countries.notes: As of Oct 2026, US outbound investment rules restrict US LPs and investors in AI, semiconductors and quantum, so most new money is RMB and state-guided. Government calls are mostly Chinese-only and published per city or district. Fund check sizes are rarely published. Web search was exhausted during research, so several entities were verified by direct site checks only.

countries.summary: Large engineering talent base centred on Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv and Dnipro; known for Grammarly, GitLab (co-founded), MacPaw and Preply. Since 2022 the ecosystem has pivoted strongly to defence tech, supported by the state Brave1 cluster and a wave of defence-focused funds.
countries.company_setup: LLC (TOV) or sole proprietor (FOP); online registration via Diia for residents, foreigners usually register via a notary or representative. IT firms can join the Diia.City special regime (9% tax on withdrawn capital or 18% CIT, 5% PIT for staff). Many founders also use a Delaware, UK, Polish or Estonian parent.
countries.notes: Wartime context (since Feb 2022): martial law, power and security risks; defence tech dominates new funding. Seeds of Bravery (EIC-funded) has concluded. Star Venture Ukraine intake deadline 2026-10-30 per EU Neighbours East notice. USF Startup EDGE page says next call coming soon. EIC 2027 cut-offs to be published 2026-11-19. Several VC check sizes come from secondary sources.

countries.summary: Largest startup ecosystem in the world, centered on the San Francisco Bay Area, New York, Boston, Los Angeles, Austin and Seattle. It leads in AI, software, biotech and defense tech, with the deepest VC market and exits such as Google, Meta, Uber, Airbnb and OpenAI's growth.
countries.startup_visa: No dedicated startup visa. International Entrepreneur Parole (IER, Form I-941, needs ~US$311k qualified investment or ~US$124k government grant; DHS has signalled rescission), plus O-1, H-1B, E-2 and EB-5 routes. https://www.uscis.gov/working-in-the-united-states/international-entrepreneur-rule
countries.company_setup: Delaware C-corp is standard for VC-backed startups. Foreigners can incorporate remotely (e.g. Stripe Atlas, Clerky) for a few hundred US$ in 1-3 days; EIN and US bank account are possible without residency.
countries.notes: SBIR/STTR lapsed 2025-10-01 and was reauthorized 2026-04-13 through 2031-09-30; agencies are still rebuilding solicitation calendars. DoD FY27 Release 1 opens 2026-10-28 and closes 2026-11-25 (from secondary source). International Entrepreneur Parole remains on USCIS site but rescission has been signalled. Web search budget ran out mid-research, so some state programs (Colorado, Maryland TEDCO, NY) were left out and some accelerator deadlines remain unknown; VC check sizes left as unknown.

countries.summary: Small, recovering ecosystem in Caracas. A 2026 market map counts about 105 active startups. Casa212 offers a US$150k founder residency, the first Venezuela Tech Week ran in May 2026, and the Startup Venezuela Summit runs 2026-10-21 to 23.
countries.company_setup: Compania Anonima (C.A.) registered at the Registro Mercantil (SAREN) plus RIF tax ID; slow and bureaucratic. Many founders incorporate in the US or Delaware.
countries.notes: US sanctions (OFAC) on the government and PDVSA complicate dealings with state entities and banking, as of Oct 2026. Most founders use offshore holding companies. Venezuela is an IDB member but IDB lending has been frozen for years. The FONACIT site was unreachable.

countries.summary: Fast-growing ecosystem in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi with strong engineering talent; notable companies include VNG, MoMo, Sky Mavis and VNLife. Government backing via the National Innovation Center (NIC) and the National Technology Innovation Fund.

countries.notes: SIHUB (Ho Chi Minh City) and Nextrans sites could not be resolved in Oct 2026 and are omitted. No startup visa; foreign-owned company setup is slow.

countries.notes: Ongoing civil war and Red Sea crisis; US sanctions and FTO designation of Ansar Allah (Houthis) complicate payments. No verified active VCs or accelerators.
